name: Paulohi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_quote: Der Ton ruht in der Regel auf der vorletzten Silbe; treten Suffixe an den Wortstamm, so rückt der Accent um so viele Silben nach hinten, als das Suffix deren enthält: fále vier, falé-ma wir vier; nife Zahn, nife-níru ihre Zähne. Die Beeinflussung der Accentuierung ist ein sicheres Kennzeichen zur Unterscheidung der Suffixe von nachgesetzten Partikeln.

audit.reasoning: The classification fixed-strict penultimate (penultimate stress) with domain word matches Stresemann §10 exactly: stress on the penult, shifting rightward with suffixes (fále / falé-ma, nífe / nife-níru), with a closed list of ten oxytone lexical exceptions in §11 and §2 calling Paulohi words 'Paroxytona mit verschwindenden Ausnahmen'. The quotation is verbatim in the Google Books scan we hold at the stated section and page. The source is a full reference grammar with a dedicated accent section, it is the sole description of a language moribund since 1899, and the secondary database (StressTyp2) cites the same work. Nothing better exists to download; list of works to obtain empty. Minor housekeeping only: the record's 'quote'/'cite'/'loc'/'grade' fields are blank while the content sits in 'the domain quotation'/'the domain locator'/'sources' — worth populating, but not an evidence problem.

sources.quote: §10: "The stress rests as a rule on the penultimate syllable; if suffixes attach to the word stem, the accent moves as many syllables toward the end as the suffix contains: fále 'four', falé-ma 'we four'; nife 'tooth', nife-níru 'their teeth'. This effect on accentuation is a sure mark for distinguishing suffixes from postposed particles." §11: "The following words exceptionally carry the accent on the final vowel: arapá 'to joke', aséh 'to breathe', fué 'hither', kipulá 'midnight', kokoté 'to c

sources.note: Not opened (print; no digitised copy found): a Lautlehre of the Ambon-Seram languages built largely on Paulohi data; Collins 1983 cites it for stress-conditioned vowel loss and vowel splits (e.g. 1927:42 'because of stress as Stresemann noted', Sub-Buru loss of the vowel preceding the stressed syllable), so it contains statements on word accent (Betonung) in these languages; expected to restate penultimate accent for Paulohi as in Stresemann 1918 §10 and to say nothing of lexical tone. No tone statement can be attributed until the Beiheft is seen.
